question: A man goes to Mumbai from Pune at a speed of 78km/hr and returns to Pune at speed of 91km/hr, through same route. What is his average speed (in km/hr) of the entire journey?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a person covers two equal distances at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Given speeds are x = 78 km/hr and y = 91 km/hr.

Average Speed = (2 × 78 × 91) ÷ (78 + 91)

Average Speed = (2 × 78 × 91) ÷ 169

Average Speed = 2 × 6 × 7 = 84 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 84 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed from Pune to Mumbai = 78 km/hr

Speed from Mumbai to Pune = 91 km/hr

 Constant Distance (D)

**Formula Used:**

Average speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the one-way distance be the LCM of the speeds (78 and 91) to simplify calculations.

⇒ 78 = 13 × 6 and 91 = 13 × 7

⇒ LCM of 78 and 91 = 13 × 6 × 7 = 546

⇒ Let the distance between Pune and Mumbai be 546 km.

⇒ Time taken from Pune to Mumbai = Distance ÷ Speed = 546 ÷ 78 = 7 hours.

⇒ Time taken from Mumbai to Pune = Distance ÷ Speed = 546 ÷ 91 = 6 hours.

⇒ Total Distance covered = 546 + 546 = 1092 km.

⇒ Total Time taken = 7 + 6 = 13 hours.

⇒ Average Speed = 1092 ÷ 13 = 84 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 84 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Different Distances

When travelling different distances D₁, D₂ at speeds S₁, S₂ respectively, Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time) = (D₁ + D₂) ÷ (D₁/S₁ + D₂/S₂).

Average Speed for 3 Equal Distances

When a person travels 3 equal distances at speeds x, y, and z, the Average Speed = 3xyz ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). When moving in the same direction, it is the difference (S₁ − S₂).
